observations.text: SP, due to a non-standardized clearing technique as Leader, did not continuously check the airspace for the period in charge of the formation, keeping the scan inside the cockpit for extended intervals during the rejoin and in the landing pattern. Nearby flying A/Cs were not located timely and the proper separation was not maintained. The IP had to direct the lookout and to take the controls in order to avoid converging traffic, so the item could not be completed without assistance.

SP, due to attention captured by a minor cockpit indication while the outside picture went unmonitored, did not divide attention appropriately between the work inside and outside the cockpit and did not apply admissible clearing techniques during the fingertip turn. An A/C crossing the working area was not conceived as a potential hazard and no flight parameter was regulated to avoid it. The IP called the traffic and directed the avoidance turn, and clearing was thereafter performed only under IP direction.

SP, due to a clearing technique that did not cover the sectors corresponding to the relative position as No2, did not clear towards the Leader during fingertip and left the outside sector unchecked for long intervals. Traffic in the landing pattern was located only after the IP's verbal indications and the proper separation was re-established with delay. The item was completed, but recognition and correction depended on verbal prompting.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on final, did not monitor the transmissions of the other formation in the pattern and did not build an explicit perception of the traffic situation. The conflicting A/C on the initial was identified only after the IP pointed it out, and the R/T call for separation was made with delay. Separation was finally created, but only after the IP's verbal indications.

SP performed clearing within the standards for the Training Section, both as Leader and as No2, but on two occasions the scan remained inside the cockpit longer than the phase of flight required during the setup for the rejoin. On each occasion the nearby A/Cs were located and the proper separation was maintained without IP intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a more systematic division of attention between the instruments and the outside sectors is expected to improve.

SP continuously checked the airspace for the full period in charge of the formation and, as No2, cleared towards the Leader during fingertip, dividing attention between the visual and the R/T stimuli in an accurate and timely manner. Nearby flying A/Cs were located early, potential hazards were conceived and the flight parameters were regulated to preserve the proper separation, without any IP intervention. The R/T was used effectively to create safe separation from the traffic in the landing pattern. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP applied admissible clearing techniques with exceptional accuracy throughout the sortie, maintaining an uninterrupted check of the airspace as Leader and a correctly oriented scan towards the Leader as No2, with negligible interruptions of the outside picture. All traffic in the working area and in the landing pattern was located well before it became a factor, and the flight parameters and the R/T calls were used to preserve separation without any prompting. The perception of the position of the formation relative to the surrounding traffic was maintained above the desired levels for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a clearing scan restricted to the area ahead of the nose, did not check the sectors of responsibility as Leader and did not clear the direction of turn before initiating the formation turn. An A/C at the same level inside the working area was not located and the proper separation was not maintained. The IP directed the lookout and executed the avoidance turn, and clearing could not be sustained without assistance for the remainder of the sortie.

SP, due to an unagreed division of lookout responsibility within the formation, did not execute clearing according to the relative position as No2 and left the sector away from the Leader uncovered. Traffic entering the pattern was not perceived and no supporting call was passed to No1, who retained the main responsibility without any support. The IP had to assume the clearing task and to direct the repositioning of the formation.

SP, due to a clearing sequence that was not adapted to the phase of flight, did not intensify the check of the airspace in the landing pattern and did not scan the sector towards the Leader before the turn to the break. The preceding A/C in the pattern was located only after the IP's verbal indication and the interval was corrected with delay. The proper separation was finally maintained, but recognition and correction were late and prompted.

SP, due to complacency in a familiar pattern that replaced an active scan, did not conceive the developing conflict with the preceding formation as a potential hazard and did not regulate the flight parameters in time. The situation was recognized only after the IP's verbal indications and the extension of the downwind was applied with delay. Separation was restored, but the reaction depended entirely on IP prompting.

SP, due to a scan cycle that dwelt on the instruments during the rejoin, did not check the outside sectors at the required rate and momentarily lost visual contact with the crossing traffic reported on the R/T. The A/C was reacquired by SP and the proper separation was maintained throughout. The minor deviation of the clearing pattern was recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during the entry to the working area, did not monitor the radio transmissions of the other formation for a short interval and did not hold an explicit perception of the traffic situation. The position of the other formation was rebuilt from the following calls and the check of the airspace was resumed at the correct rate. The minor lapse was recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP's intervention and without any verbal indication.

SP executed clearing within the standards for the Training Section, dividing attention between the visual and the R/T stimuli and maintaining the proper separation from the surrounding traffic. However, on two occasions as Leader the check of the airspace behind the formation was performed later than the phase of flight required, without the separation being affected. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a steadier scan rate in the turns and in the landing pattern is expected to improve.

SP maintained an uninterrupted check of the airspace for the full period in charge of the formation, with the clearing pattern adapted to the phase of flight and, as No2, correctly oriented towards the Leader during fingertip. All nearby A/Cs were located early, potential hazards were conceived in advance and both the flight parameters and the R/T were used to create safe separation, with negligible interruptions of the outside scan. Attention was divided between the work inside and outside the cockpit with exceptional accuracy, above the desired levels for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.
